title: Bumps: Redcoats
subtitle: Lady Margaret on the Cam. Catch the boat ahead before the boat behind catches you.
controls: Each oar has its own key, shuffled every race. Press a key to pull that oar. Pull both sides together or the boat turns.
start: Press any oar key to sit ready
restart: Space, Enter or click to race again

stations.name: Baitsbite Lock
stations.fact: In the bumps, crews start in a line, one and a half lengths apart, and set off together on the gun.

stations.name: First Post Corner
stations.fact: A bump is any contact between your boat and the boat ahead. Both crews then pull in to the bank.

stations.name: Grassy Corner
stations.fact: The Lady Margaret Boat Club is the boat club of St John's College, founded in 1825.

stations.name: Plough Reach
stations.fact: LMBC rowers wear bright red jackets. The story goes that they were so blazing red they gave us the word blazer.

stations.name: Ditton Corner
stations.fact: Bank parties cycle the towpath blowing whistles: one for a length and a half, two for a length, three for half a length, and a long blast when you are about to bump.

stations.name: Long Reach
stations.fact: The Lent Bumps are in Lent term. The May Bumps are in June, because Cambridge.

stations.name: Railway Bridge
stations.fact: A crew that bumps wears willow in their hair, and the cox carries a sprig back on the boat.

stations.name: Top Finish
stations.fact: Early SBR members, in gowns after dinner, 'accidentally' sank passing punts and then retired to the Samuel Butler Room for coffee.

cox: Same time, same oar, same boat, please.
Somebody is rowing with their eyes shut. Several somebodies.
Remember why you came to Cambridge. Not for this.
Bow side, are you with us?
Stroke side, are you with us?
Think of the Buttery. Pull for the Buttery.
This is costing the boat club money.
coxClose: Half a length! Give me ten!
I can smell their sun cream. Go!
Their cox is looking at us. Make them regret it!
They are crumbling. Do not crumble with them.
coxChased: Do not look behind you. They are right behind you.
Bank party says they are gaining. I say pull.
Somebody has to get bumped today. Make it them.
crashes: Into the reeds. The swans are judging you.
Beached. The towpath cyclists applaud ironically.
That bank was in the plan, apparently.
Pushing off with an oar. Very traditional.
The cox would like everyone to know it was not the steering.
bumpLines: Willow all round. Somebody tell the Buttery.
A clean bump. Their cox is putting a brave face on it.
Contact! Lady Margaret goes up a place.
caughtLines: {crew} bump you. Your cox raises a hand, very gracious, very sad.
Bumped. The boat club will be writing to you.
You go down a place. The bank party pretends not to know you.
rowOverLines: Rowed over. Nobody caught anybody and everyone is tired.
You row over. Respectable, which is the worst thing to be in the bumps.
prizeHint: Willow for the crew. Drag a sprig into someone's hair.
prizeLines: {name} ({role}) now looks like a very successful hedge.
Willow in the hair of {name}. The {role} portfolio has never looked better.
{name} ({role}) will be finding leaves until Easter.
prizeNoRoster: Your cox wears the willow with pride.
